name: Cable Shotgun Row
summary: A standing unilateral cable row performed from a split stance, rotating the grip from neutral or pronated to supinated to target the lats.

setup: Attach a single D-handle to a cable pulley set to the lowest position.
Grasp the handle with one hand and step back into a stable split stance with the foot opposite your working arm forward.
Hinge slightly forward at the hips while keeping your chest proud and core braced.
steps: Allow your working arm to extend fully toward the pulley, letting the scapula gently protract to stretch the lat.
Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blade and driving your elbow down and back toward your hip.
Rotate your forearm as you pull, turning your palm upward into supination as the handle approaches your torso.
Pause briefly at peak contraction, squeezing the lat without twisting your torso.
Lower the weight with control by reversing the motion, extending the arm and rotating back to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you row the handle toward your hip, and inhale as you return the cable under control.
cues: Drive your elbow to your hip pocket.
Turn the palm up as you pull.
Keep your shoulders and hips square.

common_faults.fault: Over-rotating the torso to heave the weight back.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core and keep the chest facing forward, isolating movement to the arm and shoulder blade.

common_faults.fault: Flaring the elbow out wide away from the body.
common_faults.correction: Keep the elbow path tight to your ribs to direct tension into the lower and mid lat.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear during the row.
common_faults.correction: Keep the shoulder depressed and pull down and back rather than upward.

precautions: Maintain a stable split stance to prevent losing balance as fatigue sets in.
